meal.name: Porchetta Dinner
meal.workflow_md:
## Menu *3 pax + leftovers · 26 June 2026* 1. Porchetta with Salsa Verde 2. Crispy Roast Potatoes with Garlic, Lemon Zest & Flaky Salt 3. Charred Radicchio & Raw Fennel Salad 4. Warm Cannellini Beans with Garlic & Olive Oil 5. Chilled Orange with Olive Oil & Flaky Salt > *Portion note: Potatoes and beans together are substantial. For lighter appetites, omit one or the other — if retaining only one, keep the salad.* ## Critical Path > ***Critical path:** Rendering complete before crackling phase → crackling phase → 30-minute steam-free rest governs service. Do not delay slicing for side synchronisation. If crackling runs long, sacrifice potato crispness and bean temperature — protect crackling integrity and pork temperature.* ## T-Minus Timeline
TimeAction
T−24 to T−18Salt and roll porchetta. Tie every 2.5 cm. Salt skin. Air-dry uncovered on rack over tray in refrigerator.
T−2:45Begin rendering phase — oven 300°F / 150°C, middle rack, elevated wire rack over tray. (1 hr 45 min–2 hr 10 min)
T−2:00Reserve 45–60 ml / 3–4 tbsp rendered pork fat from drip tray for potatoes.
T−1:05Start beans on Burner 1. Make salsa verde. Char radicchio cut-side down in cast-iron on Burner 2 (60–90 sec). Slice fennel thinly.
T−0:55Parboil potatoes in well-salted water on Burner 2 — 12–14 min (outer layer yields, centre still firm).
T−0:52Raise oven to 475°F / 245°C. Crackling phase begins. (15–25 min)
T−0:42Drain potatoes. Rough surfaces aggressively in pot until shaggy. Hold uncovered on tray — 10 min surface drying before oven entry.
T−0:32Remove porchetta. Rest uncovered on elevated rack (30 min — do not tent). Potatoes enter oven immediately in reserved pork fat at 475°F / 245°C.
T−0:10Remove potatoes. Hold uncovered on rack.
T−0:04Zest and juice Lemon 2. Dress salad. Final seasoning on beans.
T−0:02Finish potatoes with lemon zest and flaky salt. Slice porchetta (remove twine; 1–1.5 cm slices).
T−0:00SERVE — Beans → Potatoes → Porchetta → Salsa verde → Salad. Window: 5–7 min. First failure if delayed: crackling softens.
**Critical path:** *Rendering must be complete before crackling phase — premature high heat is the primary failure mode. Once oven raises to 475°F at T−0:52, potatoes hold dry on tray. Porchetta 30-minute rest is non-negotiable; do not begin slicing before T−0:02.* ## Oven Sequencing & Heat Allocation **Oven sequencing:** *300°F / 150°C for rendering (Burner 1: beans; Burner 2: potato parboil from T−0:55, cast-iron radicchio char at T−1:05 clears well before parboil). Raise to 475°F / 245°C at T−0:52 for crackling. Oven remains at 475°F continuously through potato roast — no second transition. Potatoes enter the vacated oven at T−0:32 at full temperature.* ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDrift RiskCorrective Action
PorchettaElevated rack, uncovered, airflow underneath30 minCrackling softensReturn uncovered to 475°F / 245°C for 5–7 min before slicing
PotatoesUncovered on rack, room temp10–15 minCrust softens progressivelyNo recovery — serve as promptly as possible; never cover
BeansCovered on very low heat30 minTighten and thickenLoosen with 1–2 tbsp warm water before serving
SaladUndressed, refrigeratedUntil T−0:04Wilting if dressed earlyDress only at T−0:04 — never before
Salsa verdeRoom temperature, covered2 hoursHerb oxidation over timePrepare at T−1:05; use within 2 hours
## Sourcing Notes *Sourcing: One parsley bunch covers salsa verde (20 g). Lemon 1 zested at assembly (T−24); Lemon 2 zested and juiced at service (T−0:04) — do not zest in advance. Olive oil: ~190 ml total, one 500 ml bottle covers all dishes.*
meal.shared_prep_md:
**Lemons — 2 total:** prep differs by timing.

Lemon 1: zest only → Porchetta paste (at roll assembly, T−24 to T−18).

Lemon 2: zest of ½ → Potato finish; juice of ½ → Salad dressing. Both at service — zest and juice Lemon 2 together at T−0:04.

**Garlic — 13 medium cloves + 1 small:** prep differs per dish, do not aggregate.

6 cloves → Porchetta paste (process with herbs) · 3 cloves → Potatoes (crush lightly, add halfway through roast) · 3 cloves → Beans (slice thin at T−1:05) · 1 small clove → Salsa verde (mince fine at T−1:05)

dishes.name: Porchetta with Salsa Verde
dishes.summary: Skin-on pork belly rolled around a centre-cut loin with a fennel-herb paste, dry-brined 18–30 h, rendered at 300°F / 150°C then blistered at 475°F / 245°C to 142°F / 61°C, rested 30 min uncovered and served with a parsley-mint-caper salsa verde.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Three-texture porchetta — shattered crackling, rendered belly fat, juicy loin centre — with mandatory salsa verde delivering the meal's primary acid balance and preventing palate fatigue across a full serving. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: 6–8 · Total: ~24 hr (incl. drying) · Active: ~35 min · Oven: 300°F → 475°F / 150°C → 245°C · Rest: 30 min* ## Prep Phase > *Critical path: full fat rendering before blistering phase. Overnight drying is non-negotiable. Salsa verde prepared at T−1:05 during rendering.* 1. **Belly:** Butterfly thicker areas to create an even slab ~1.5 cm / 0.6 in throughout. Make shallow horizontal cuts through thick interior sections only — do not cut through skin. Verify thickness end-to-end. Pat completely dry. 2. **Loin:** Trim silver skin. Orient loin so its grain runs parallel to the long axis of the roll — crosswise slicing at carving cuts across the grain of both belly and loin simultaneously. 3. **Salt cure:** Rub 18 g salt directly onto meat surfaces of both belly and loin. Rest 30–60 min refrigerated. 4. **Paste:** Combine fennel seed, peppercorns, garlic, rosemary, sage, lemon zest, chili flakes, olive oil. Process to a coarse paste. 5. **Assemble:** Rub paste over meat surfaces. Centre loin on belly. Roll tightly skin-side out. Tie every 2.5 cm / 1 in with butcher's twine. 6. **Dry-brine:** Rub skin with 8 g salt. Place uncovered on wire rack over tray in refrigerator 18–30 hours. Before roasting: skin must feel dry and tacky — not damp or cool. If moisture beads remain, continue drying. ## Active Cooking **Temper** Remove from refrigerator 60 min before roasting. Pat skin dry. Rub with neutral oil. Optional for weaker ovens: skewer perforations through skin every 2–3 cm / 1 in — do not deeply score. **Rendering Phase — 300°F / 150°C** Middle rack, elevated wire rack over tray. Cook until loin centre reaches 130°F / 54°C and fat beneath skin appears translucent rather than opaque white. Approx. 1 hr 45 min–2 hr 10 min. Secondary cue: fat feels softened rather than rubbery when pressed lightly with tongs — if still firm and opaque, continue. **Crackling Phase — 475°F / 245°C** Roast 15–25 min, rotating as needed. Pull when crackling is deeply blistered and audibly crisp when tapped, and loin centre reaches 142°F / 61°C. Carryover: final ~145°F / 63°C. Secondary cue: probe enters loin centre with light resistance like warm butter — springy or tight means continue. ## Holding & Assembly Rest uncovered on elevated wire rack over tray or board — 30 minutes. Do not tent. Trapped steam softens crackling; elevated airflow prevents underside steaming. If crackling softens during rest: return uncovered to 475°F / 245°C for 5–7 min before slicing. Salsa verde: finely chop parsley, mint, capers, garlic. Combine with vinegar, oil, salt, pepper. Hold at room temperature up to 2 hours. Remove twine. Slice 1–1.5 cm / 0.4–0.6 in. Serve immediately with salsa verde. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalWet skin entering oven — skin feels damp or cool rather than dry and tacky before roastingExtend uncovered refrigeration 6–12 h; unrecoverable once roasting begins
CriticalHigh heat before full rendering — fat layer opaque white and firm at start of crackling phaseReturn to 300°F / 150°C; continue until fat turns translucent and softens; retry crackling phase
MajorLoose rolling — visible gaps or movement inside roll when lifted before roastingRe-roll and re-tie tightly before roasting
MajorExcessive blistering — skin transitions to dark mahogany with acrid aroma during crackling phaseRemove immediately; lightly scrape isolated burnt spots if limited in area
## Adjustment Notes ***Adjust:** Increase salsa verde quantity if pork reads heavy; add additional salsa verde at the plate rather than applying citrus directly to the meat.*

dishes.name: Crispy Roast Potatoes with Garlic, Lemon Zest & Flaky Salt
dishes.summary: Parboiled and roughed Yukon Gold chunks roasted 20–30 min at 475°F / 245°C in fat reserved from the porchetta, with crushed garlic added halfway and finished with lemon zest and flaky salt.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Crisp starch contrast cooked in reserved pork fat; lemon zest at finish adds aromatic brightness without introducing another sauce. ## Yield & Timing *with Garlic, Lemon Zest & Flaky Salt · Yield: 3–4 · Parboil: 12–14 min · Roast: 20–30 min at 475°F / 245°C* ## Prep Phase Cut into large chunks. Parboil in well-salted water 12–14 min until outer layer yields easily, centre still firm. Drain. Rough surfaces aggressively in pot until edges look shaggy. Hold uncovered on tray — 10 min surface drying before oven entry. Do not cover. ## Active Cooking Roast at 475°F / 245°C in reserved pork fat, 20–30 min. Add crushed garlic halfway through. Stop when deep golden crust forms and potatoes are audibly crisp when shaken in tray. ## Holding & Assembly Hold uncovered on rack up to 10–15 min. Finish with finely grated lemon zest and flaky salt immediately before serving. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalInsufficient roughing — smooth potato exterior after draining with no shaggy edges; crust will be thin and weakReturn to pot; shake vigorously until surfaces look shaggy before roasting

dishes.name: Charred Radicchio & Raw Fennel Salad
dishes.summary: Radicchio quarters charred 60–90 sec cut-side down in cast-iron, combined with mandoline-thin raw fennel and dressed at T−0:04 with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Bitterness, crunch, and temperature contrast — raw fennel brings volatile anise freshness structurally distinct from the porchetta's toasted fennel seed. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: 3 · Prep: 15 min · Active: 5 min · Dress at service only* ## Prep Phase Quarter radicchio through the core. Slice fennel very thinly on a mandoline or by hand. Refrigerate undressed until T−0:04. ## Active Cooking Heat a cast-iron pan over high heat until very hot. Place radicchio quarters cut-side down. Char 60–90 sec without moving. Remove when outer leaves lightly charred but interior structure remains firm. ## Holding & Assembly Combine charred radicchio and raw fennel. Dress immediately before serving with olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorOvercooking radicchio — collapsed leaves, no crunch remaining; monitoring required at 60 secondsUnrecoverable; monitor closely during char
## Adjustment Notes ***Adjust:** Increase lemon juice if salad reads too bitter.*

designed_unvalidated.note: Monitor at 60 seconds; collapse is unrecoverable.

dishes.name: Warm Cannellini Beans with Garlic & Olive Oil
dishes.summary: Tinned cannellini beans warmed 8–10 min in olive oil with thin-sliced garlic sweated 2–3 min without browning; holds covered on very low heat up to 30 min.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Soft earthy buffer that absorbs pork juices on the plate without introducing creaminess or competing with either crisp component. ## Yield & Timing *with Garlic & Olive Oil · Yield: 3–4 · Prep: 5 min · Active: 15 min · Hold: 30 min max* ## Prep Phase Drain and rinse beans. Slice garlic thin. ## Active Cooking Heat olive oil over medium-low. Cook garlic until translucent and fragrant, 2–3 min — no browning. Add beans; warm through 8–10 min until some beans begin lightly collapsing at the edges. ## Holding & Assembly Hold covered on very low heat up to 30 min. If beans tighten, loosen with 1–2 tbsp warm water before serving. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorBrowning garlic — edges darkening, aroma turns sharp before beans are addedDiscard; restart garlic in clean oil
## Adjustment Notes ***Adjust:** Add a small spoonful of salsa verde if beans read flat.*

designed_unvalidated.note: Loosen with 1–2 tbsp warm water if beans tighten.

dishes.name: Chilled Orange with Olive Oil & Flaky Salt
dishes.summary: Fully peeled orange rounds chilled 30 min minimum and finished at service with a light drizzle of good olive oil and flaky salt — a palate cleanser rather than a sweet dessert.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Cold, bitter-acid palate reset after rendered pork fat — a palate cleanser, not a conventional sweet dessert; set this expectation with guests in advance. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: 3 · Prep: 10 min · Chill: 30 min minimum* ## Prep Phase Peel oranges fully, removing all pith. Slice into rounds. Refrigerate 30 min minimum. ## Holding & Assembly Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Finish with flaky salt immediately before serving. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MinorExcess olive oil — pooling on plate, greasy mouthfeelBlot lightly with kitchen paper
